newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish government body approves sale of four firms.
newsitem.headline: Polish government body approves sale of four firms.

text.p: The Polish government's economic committee on Monday approved the privatisation of a tile-maker, a paper plant, a wholesale trader and an agricultural machine maker, the government press office said in a Monday statement.

It said the committee (KERM) recommended to the full cabinet that the Opoczno tile-maker be sold by transforming it into a joint stock company, raising its capital and selling the new issue to a strategic investor.
It said farm machine maker Fabryka Maszyn i Urzadzen Agromet-Pionier in Strzelce Opolskie needed an investor to modernise the firm because its financial situation was adequate only to pay its debts.

The statement said the Ostroleckie Zaklady Celulozowo- Papiernicze in the town of Ostroleka (OZCP) paper company also needed to be sold because for the last seven years it had been drawing its profits mainly from leasing its assets.
There was investor interest in OZCP, the statement added.

The KERM also said the Przedsiebiorstwo Hurtu Spozywczego (PHS) in the town of Szczecin should be privatised by creating a company which would lease the assets of PHS and which would be owned by PHS employees and other investors.
It did not give any other details.
